perspective:
From Ethan’s available perspective:

- Ethan knows Gary Guo as a long-time close friend from middle school; Gary is a doctor, and Ethan is a plumber.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- Ethan invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation/rejuvenation.
- Gary initially declined, saying he appreciated Ethan’s concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
- Ethan suspected there was more behind Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, reminding him they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told Ethan it was complicated and that he hadn’t wanted to burden him.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy and offered to help Gary find better balance.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities.
- Gary agreed, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary and discussed Gary’s progress and remaining challenges.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, that Ethan’s help meant he was less overwhelmed, and that he had had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- After about a year, Ethan saw/believed Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own.
- Ethan decided to step back, told Gary he was always just a call away, that he knew Gary had this, and to keep up the great work.
- Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
